_comment: GiantSpider's grown-up venom (farm-band damage fix 2026-07-22, revised the same day after live play): the cL9 GiantSpider inherited VenomSpit at level 1 — a curve-position-1 baseline authored for the cL4 tunnel VenomSpider, and the weakest baseline in the roster. Its own skill so the farm band is not chained to the tunnel baseline. TWO payloads on one aura (PO 2026-07-22, from live play: 'still a very easy win — currently it's only the dot and that hits pretty weak'): a bite that lands on the aura tick AND the venom it injects. The bite is what fixes the feel — a pure dot takes 1.5 s to deal its first point, so brief contact dealt literally zero. Both payloads are poison-tagged so Antivenom stays the counter to the WHOLE package rather than half of it. Both carry identical radius/tickInterval/maxTargets ON PURPOSE: the live mob owns ONE aura sensor sized to the max radius across effects (skills.EquippedSkill.EffectiveRadius) and target selection filters by that sensor, not per effect — divergent geometry would silently apply the smaller effect at the larger radius, so simharness auraSpecOf now hard-fails on it. At cL9 (f=2.476): bite 8.7/hit every 1.33 s = 6.5 HP/s, venom 14.9/tick every 1.5 s = 9.9 HP/s, total ~16.4 HP/s — about a 17 s kill on a facetanking cL9 player, who needs ~17 s to kill the spider back. That is ABOVE the old soft/hard cliff (9.1-10.4 HP/s): GiantSpider is deliberately no longer a facetankable normal, and the farm band's soft-normal guardrail floor was dropped to Z1/Z2 in the same pass (PO ruling: the farm band is deliberate content, it may be hard across the board). The damage only matters because speed went 0.6 -> 0.95 in the same pass — at 0.6 the mob moved at 66% of player walking speed and could never hold anyone inside its aura, so its authored DPS was unreachable by a player walking backwards.
